heading.purpose: Page title only, used once per view ("OrchestAI").

body.purpose: Default for prompts, outputs, table cells, descriptions.

label.purpose: Uppercase section eyebrows and column headers.

shadows.name: flat
shadows.purpose: Resting state for the large majority of surfaces.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Hover/active/selected cards and the raised surface tier.

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Tinted pill showing task/agent execution status (Running, Completed, Failed, Pending, Warning).
components.css: .ds-status-badge { background: rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.18); color: #7aa2f7; border: 1px solid rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.55); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 10px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { width: 100%; padding: 9px 0; border-radius: 6px; border: none; background: #89b4fa; color: #1e1e2e; font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #a9c7fb; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { background: #313244; color: #6c7086; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #89b4fa; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Panel Card
components.description: Standard content panel (used throughout Observability views) — base background, surface0 border, 8px radius.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: #1e1e2e; border: 1px solid #313244; border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px 18px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-panel-label { font-size: 10px; color: #6c7086; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-panel-value { font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; color: #cdd6f4; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', 'Fira Code', monospace; }

components.name: Status-Accented Card
components.description: Agent execution / approval / manager-review card — the one deliberate exception to the side-stripe-border ban, using a 3px colored left border to attach a status color to the whole card.
components.css: .ds-status-card { border: 1px solid rgba(22, 163, 74, 0.25); border-left: 3px solid #16a34a; border-radius: 8px; padding: 12px 14px; background: #1e1e2e; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; } .ds-status-card-title { color: #cdd6f4; font-size: 14px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard text/textarea field used in the task submission form.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 7px 10px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid #313244; background: #1e1e2e; color: #cdd6f4; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', 'Fira Code', monospace; outline: none; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #6c7086; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #89b4fa; }

narrative.overview: OrchestAI's frontend is not a dashboard you browse — it's a console you read. Every screen exists to answer one question fast: what happened, why, how much did it cost, how do I reproduce it. The visual language follows from that job directly: a two-face type system (a proportional UI face — IBM Plex Sans — for chrome/prose, monospace — JetBrains Mono — reserved for the raw data: IDs, timestamps, durations, cost figures, code/JSON, span IDs, because a proportional font really would be lying about what that content is), a Catppuccin Mocha dark base with a genuine, restrained surface hierarchy (canvas -> surface -> raised -> overlay) and a small disciplined elevation scale (flat -> raised -> overlay), and a deliberately narrow, dense information architecture that packs execution data close together rather than spacing it out for comfort. This system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS dashboard: no gradient hero metrics, no cream/sand card grids, no rounded pastel "consumer analytics" look. An engineer debugging a failed multi-agent run at 2am should feel like they're reading htop or a Grafana Tempo trace view, not browsing a Stripe-dashboard-clone. The R1 ("Design-System Foundation") redesign sharpens this identity — real type hierarchy, real surface depth, restrained shadows — it does not soften it toward generic SaaS. Canonical element -> face mapping (P2-M2's governing rule): UI face (IBM Plex Sans) = navigation, headings, section titles, labels, buttons, instruction/prose copy, status messages, chrome; data face (JetBrains Mono) = IDs, timestamps, durations, cost figures, any numeric value, code/JSON, technical/trace/span IDs, data table cells. Four standing decisions: (1) the app-shell default (#root in index.css) stays JetBrains Mono, the data-safe fallback for anything not yet assigned a role; (2) typography.body (theme/tokens.js) stays on the data face, unchanged, until Phase 2's per-element split reassigns individual call sites; (3) UI prose renders via a UI-face role/token (typeScale.body or equivalent), never the legacy mono typography.body, once a component migrates; (4) within Input/TextArea, the field content stays mono while its label is UI face. Rollout note (R1 partial-baseline -> P2-M2 completing the split): the `components` CSS samples below depict each control's intended end-state face per the Two-Face Rule (e.g. a button label in IBM Plex Sans). At the R1 partial-baseline the only shared controls actually rendering the UI face were those consuming the `label` role token (Label, StatusBadge) plus the new role-authored primitives; every other control — including bare headings — inherited the JetBrains Mono app-shell face (#root in index.css, plus index.css's bare h1/h2 rule). P2-M2 Task A1 closes the heading piece of that residual baseline: bare h1/h2 headings now default to the UI face (index.css's new --ui var) since a heading is never a rendered data value; #root's mono default is deliberately unchanged. The remaining mono-inheriting controls (Button, NavItem, Input/TextArea, StateText, and Panel/Card chrome) still inherit #root's mono face today — migrating each is Task A2 (shared components), with Task B completing the sweep per-surface — so a sample showing the UI face on a button label still describes the target, not yet the rendering, until A2 lands (documented "residual mono UI text" narrowing task-by-task, not a defect).
keyCharacteristics: Two-face typography: IBM Plex Sans (self-hosted) for UI chrome — headings, titles, labels, navigation, prose — JetBrains Mono (self-hosted) reserved for data — IDs, timestamps, durations, cost figures, code/JSON, span IDs.

Layered, not flat: a 4-tier surface ramp (canvas -> surface -> raised -> overlay) and a small 3-step elevation scale (flat -> raised -> overlay) replace the old two-flat-layer/zero-shadow model, still restrained — no dramatic drop-shadows.
Dense: type scale spans 10-28px (display -> caption), tight padding, small-to-medium radii (3-12px)

Two distinct color roles never blended: soft Catppuccin tones identify what (agent type, structural UI), harder saturated tones identify state (status badges, and — via documented alias, not new hues — non-status semantic UI like toasts/banners)

rules.name: The Two-Palette Rule
rules.body: Identity (which agent, which color role in the UI) is always a Catppuccin tone. State (is this run running / done / failed) is always drawn from the harder Status set. Never use Alert Red for a "Failed" badge or Status Failed for inline error text. The good/warn/critical semantic aliases are Status-set colors reused under a non-status name — they do not create a third palette.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Trace Blue is the only color used for interactive affordances (buttons, links, focus). It appears on a small fraction of any screen; its rarity is what makes it register as "click here" rather than decoration. Explicitly re-validated (not just carried forward) at R1 via a dense synthetic palette-density stress test.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Supersedes the old No-Serif Rule. Exactly two typefaces exist in this system, split by role: IBM Plex Sans for UI chrome, JetBrains Mono for data. Never introduce a third typeface. Never render IDs/timestamps/durations/costs/code/JSON in the UI face. Canonical mapping: UI face = navigation/headings/section titles/labels/buttons/instruction-prose/status messages/chrome; data face = IDs/timestamps/durations/cost figures/any numeric value/code-JSON/technical-trace-span IDs/data table cells. Standing decisions: #root's mono default is the data-safe fallback and stays unchanged; typography.body stays data-face; UI prose uses a UI-face role/token, never legacy mono typography.body; Input/TextArea field content is mono while its label is UI face.

rules.name: The Disciplined-Elevation Rule
rules.body: Supersedes the old Flat-By-Default Rule. Every shadow used in the product must be one of the three documented elevation-scale steps (flat/raised/overlay) — no arbitrary or decorative drop-shadows. The colored left-border (3px) on status-carrying cards remains a separate, still-valid convention.

dos: Do use the UI face (IBM Plex Sans) for chrome — headings, titles, labels, nav, prose — and the data face (JetBrains Mono) for IDs/timestamps/durations/costs/code/JSON. Never the reverse.
Do use the Two-Palette Rule: Catppuccin tones for identity, hard Status tones for state; good/warn/critical are Status-set colors reused for non-status UI, not a third palette.
Do use tinted-pill badges (20% alpha bg, 50–60% alpha border, full-opacity text) for any new status indicator, matching the existing badge pattern exactly.
Do reserve the 3px border-left accent for cards that represent a single dominant status; it is the one deliberate exception to the side-stripe ban below.
Do use the Surface Hierarchy (canvas/surface/raised/overlay) for background layering and the Elevation scale (flat/raised/overlay) for shadows — together, not interchangeably.
Do give every interactive element a visible :focus-visible ring (2px solid Trace Blue, 2px offset) — accessibility is a first-class acceptance criterion.
Do keep type sizes in the 10–20px range for standard UI (the full scale runs display(28px) -> caption(10px)); reserve 20px+ for the single page heading/display role only.
donts: Don't introduce a gradient, hero metric, or cream/sand card grid — this is a tracing tool, not a marketing-adjacent SaaS dashboard.
Don't use border-left as a colored accent on anything other than a status-carrying card.
Don't add a box-shadow outside the three documented elevation steps (flat/raised/overlay) — no arbitrary or dramatic depth.
Don't mix Catppuccin soft tones and hard Status tones on the same semantic concept.
Don't introduce a third typeface, or render data (IDs/timestamps/durations/costs/code/JSON) in the UI face.

Don't expand the 6-color Agent Identity Palette or the 5-color Status palette — R1's dense-fixture stress test validated the current breadth as sufficient; add semantic meaning via the documented good/warn/critical aliases, never a new hue.

Don't reconstruct span parent/child hierarchy from timestamps or visual proximity — it must always be driven by the actual spanId/parentSpanId data, mirroring the backend's own architectural rule (ADR-011).
